summary: feat(core/runtime): a reload can now replace the inputs a generation is built with — four new ReloadOptions, each replacing one build-time input for the generation the reload builds, and each validated exactly like the builder's counterpart before anything is swapped: WithReloadExternals replaces the injected external dependency values, WithReloadResolver replaces the ${scheme:ref} expansion resolver, and WithReloadHostFactory / WithReloadResultHostFactory replace either host factory decorator slot; a nil value is meaningful on every channel — nil externals, nil resolver and nil decorator each mean none — which is how a reload removes a decoration instead of leaving the retained one in place; the externals channel is what injects a name the running generation was not built with, so docs/guides/runtime.md no longer says Reload may not require such a value and now says the reload injects it; once the swap commits the replacement is retained, so a later Reload without the option builds with it, while an aborted reload (failed option validation, compose or swap) leaves every retained input and the serving generation untouched; core/runtime/runtime.go keeps the externals, the resolver and the two decorators as replaceable state with the field comments naming the replacing option, core/runtime/reload_test.go covers replacement of the externals (including a name the runtime was not built with) and of the resolver, both decorator slots, retention across a plain reload, clearing with nil, the abort path, and the option-validation errors that must leave the generation untouched, and docs/guides/runtime.md documents the four options with the nil-means-none rule and the retention and abort semantics; the motivating caller is craft's ReloadRuntimeWith, which feeds the merged Values into the resolver (WithReloadResolver) and the injected craft.runtime external (WithReloadExternals) and keeps them per key once the reload commits.
